subject: Engineering decisions
title: launched device-frame sessions in the Rust browser daemon (`open` without `--cdp-endpoint`)
question: What was measured for launched device-frame sessions in the Rust browser daemon (`open` without `--cdp-endpoint`)?
workload: 2026-10-06: launched device-frame sessions in the Rust browser daemon (`open` without `--cdp-endpoint`)
method: Transcribed from the cited historical record. Units and precision follow the source.
finding: Benchmark (open, navigate, eval through the CLI, then the daemon's own resident set, Chromium excluded): wall 2180 ms with the Node daemon vs 977 ms with the Rust one, daemon 187.5 MB vs 5.5 MB. Binary 3.7 MB.

rows: Decision: the nine-piece chain the plan listed, minus the parts named below, as `clis/wf/src/browser_launch.rs` on top of `clis/cdp` (`launch.rs`: find a Chromium, start it with a throwaway profile and an ephemeral DevTools port). `open` starts Chromium with the device flags (`--force-device-scale-factor`, `--disable-site-isolation-trials` and the fake media-stream flags for an emulated device), applies the context options as CDP overrides (shell viewport, pixel ratio, mobile and touch, the identity user agent with `{chrome}` filled from the browser's version, colour scheme, clipboard grants, ignored certificate errors, focus emulation), registers the bindings (`__mcpOpenedUrl`, `__mcpSetColorScheme`, `__mcpFocusChange`; a wrapper makes object payloads JSON strings, since CDP bindings carry strings) and the init scripts (opened-URL capture, fake microphone and camera, generated from the TS functions into `clis/cdp/src/js/`, and the focus script). `navigate` loads the harness page the first time (`/_mcp/device-frame?...` from the daemon itself), waits for `window.__shell`, fits the window to the device box, and applies the safe-area insets (rotated in landscape) and the full identity (platform, client-hint metadata, touch points) on the page; later navigations call `__shell.setTarget` and re-apply them. `eval`, `snapshot` and `scroll` run in the app frame (`device-frame-app`, or the editable frame inside it), as `getAppTarget` does. The mock keyboard works in the daemon's event loop: a focus change on an editable element shows it (the app frame gets `__MCP_KEYBOARD_VISIBLE__`, the mode `overlay` for iOS and `resize` otherwise, and the height 270 or 0), a blur hides it after 150 ms, and keys queued by the shell are forwarded every 100 ms.

Benchmark (open, navigate, eval through the CLI, then the daemon's own resident set, Chromium excluded): wall 2180 ms with the Node daemon vs 977 ms with the Rust one, daemon 187.5 MB vs 5.5 MB. Binary 3.7 MB.

Addendum (launched sessions): ref-based input in device-frame sessions. Element boxes inside the app frame now come from `DOM.getContentQuads` (main-frame coordinates), so `tap`, `type`, `press` and `drag` work through the harness's nested iframe. On a phone or tablet preset `tap` is a finger as in the Node daemon: a random point in the middle 60% of the visible box, held 70 to 140 ms, sent as `touchStart`/`touchEnd` (the page sees `touchstart`, `touchend`, then the emulated `mousedown`, `mouseup`, `click`); `--mouse` or a desktop preset taps with a mouse. `press` accepts focus in any frame, as the Node daemon's check does. Page-side event logs are identical between the daemons for a tap on a button and on an input, `type`, two Backspaces and a drag. Still refused on device-frame sessions: `stroke` (its touch variant), the pointer-routing retries the Node daemon does against the shell (not needed for the fixture page; a page that the shell overlays would show the difference), and platform fonts.
